title: Use prescaled inputs to verify MoE router weight placement
applies_when: A modular fused MoE prepare stage can apply router weights before a nonlinear expert, while a quantized expert kernel also accepts routing weights for its output reduction.
lesson: Trace the actual prepare, wrapper and backend arguments together. For a supported top-1 input-weighting route, compare (x,w,input=True) with (x*w,ones,input=False) using the same quantizer, expert and activation, with a nonunit w and nonzero reference. Retain unit-weight and ordinary output-weighting controls. If the backend reapplies w to the already prescaled expert output, the result is w*f(w*x). A nonlinear expert generally gives w*f(w*x) different from w^2*f(x), so a squared-weight comparison against the unscaled input can miss the mechanism. Test each supported quantization mode independently.
avoid_when: Check whether a monolithic backend owns routing internally and whether the supported dispatcher admits input weighting. The recorded B300 control covers a modular NVFP4 top-1 component with static and per-token scales. End-to-end model accuracy, parallel routing and throughput require separate evidence.

evidence.note: Pinned prepare branch multiplies the input by the route weight and constrains input weighting to top-1.
The modular FlashInfer call forwards top-k weights with the already prepared activations.
Bounded native B300 comparison retained four healthy controls and two affected assertions. Original failed the two affected assertions; repaired wrapper passed all six.
